mstts:express-as.prosody: Hey there, and welcome to this journey where we look at ourselves in a whole new light. Imagine, for a moment, stripping away everything modern about us—our gadgets, our customs, our busy routines—and seeing ourselves as just another animal on this planet. That’s the bold invitation at the heart of Desmond Morris’s The Naked Ape. Together, we’ll dive into some fascinating questions. What if we observed humans the way a zoologist would? What if our instincts, our rituals, the way we claim our space—all those things we take for granted—were seen as echoes of our animal past? Suddenly, the ordinary parts of our lives start to look a little wild, don’t they? As we explore, you’ll notice patterns that tie us to our primate relatives, but you’ll also spot what makes us truly unique. It’s not just about how we differ from other creatures, but about the deep, sometimes hidden, forces we share with them—like the origins of aggression, love, parenting, even the way we form groups. So, what does it really mean to be human? By peeling back the layers of civilization, we get a chance to rethink what drives us, and maybe see ourselves with a mix of humility and awe. If you’re ready to discover the instincts and behaviors that quietly shape who we are, let’s step into this adventure together. There’s a lot to uncover, and I can’t wait to explore it with you.
